item.title: Regulation as a Feature: The Case for AI Transparency
item.description:
Every conversation about the EU AI Act’s transparency rules starts from the same assumption: this is a cost to minimize. Add the disclosure, tick the box, move on. This framing gets the opportunity backwards. AI transparency, done properly, is a genuine competitive advantage for a small AI-using team that competes against operators who treat it as an afterthought.

The obligation, stated plainly

Article 50 of the AI Act requires providers of certain AI systems to state clearly that people interact with AI. It also requires marking of AI-generated or manipulated content, including deepfakes and AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest. These duties apply from 2 August 2026. Following the 2026 Digital Omnibus, generative AI systems already on the market before that date get an extended transitional period to 2 December 2026 to comply with the content-marking requirement specifically.
